Roast tomato, cream and basil oil.How to make it1.2kg ripe tomatoes, halved1 brown onion, quartered4 garlic cloves, unpeeled3 tbsp olive oil500ml vegetable stock1 tsp caster sugar150ml thickened cream1 cup basil leaves60ml extra virgin olive oilToss the tomatoes, onion and garlic with the olive oil and salt and roast at 220°C until soft and charred at the edges.Squeeze the garlic from its skins and blend everything with the stock and sugar until smooth.Warm through, stir in the cream and season.Blitz the basil with the extra virgin oil and a pinch of salt, and swirl over the soup in mugs.Hand it over in mugs or bowls you can drink from. No spoons.Hello Clarice chicken skin cracklingChip asks Steven for his chicken skin. Crisp chicken skin, hot honey, lemon salt.How to make it400g chicken skin, from the butcher1 tsp sea salt flakes1 lemon, zested3 tbsp honey1 tsp chilli flakes1 tsp smoked paprikaScrape any fat from the skin, lay it flat between 2 sheets of baking paper on a tray and weigh it down with a second tray.Bake at 200°C until golden and crisp right through, then drain on paper towel.Rub the salt with the lemon zest and paprika, and warm the honey with the chilli.Break into shards, drizzle with hot honey and sprinkle with the lemon salt.Garlic bread, torn by handThere were no utensils in medieval times.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.From the hearthTournament roast chicken with buttered cornSteven asks for a knife or fork. Herb-basted chicken, potatoes and sweet corn.How to make it1 whole chicken, about 1.8kg80g butter, softened3 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp thyme and rosemary, chopped1 lemon800g small potatoes, halved2 tbsp olive oil4 corn cobs, halved1 tsp smoked paprikaMash 50g butter with the garlic, herbs and lemon zest and push it under and over the chicken skin. Put the halved lemon inside.Toss the potatoes with the oil and salt around the chicken in a big roasting tin.Roast at 200°C, basting with the pan juices twice, until the juices run clear and the potatoes are golden.Boil the corn for 6 minutes, then roll in the rest of the butter with the paprika and salt.Sweet thingsPastry of the castleChip gave all the knights free cable. Apple turnovers, cinnamon sugar, cream.How to make it3 Granny Smith apples, peeled and diced40g butter60g brown sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon1 lemon, juiced2 sheets of frozen puff pastry, thawed1 egg, beaten2 tbsp raw sugar200ml thickened creamCook the apples in the butter with the brown sugar, half the cinnamon and the lemon juice until soft and sticky, then cool.Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, spoon apple onto each, fold into triangles and press the edges with a fork.Brush with egg, sprinkle with raw sugar and the rest of the cinnamon and bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.Whip the cream softly and serve with the warm turnovers.Mugs and cupsA mug of ale for me and me mateChip orders ale for him and his mate.
